content.$t: When Chris Colohan recently told me that something he was involved in was coming out soon and that I would probably dig it, I knew I was in for a treat. That treat came in the form of SCRAPE, an old/new project/band that consists of former members of Left for Dead, Cursed, Lifespite, Insult, Citizens Patrol, Blind to Faith, and Abusive Forms etc etc. This thing has been in the works for a while, starting back in the Covid days and slowly pieced together in the years since. Their debut self title 7" recently came out on Oblivion Records which you can hear and buy below. Chris was right, this is definitely up my alley. Self described as Iron Monkey/Unsane worship", i will add my 2 cents in and say it's got a Burning Love vibe if Burning Love was slower, darker, suffocating, sludgier, and much much uglier. Just like the world we are currently living in. There's a great review/interview over at No Echo that you should check out where the band lets slip that "there are more songs written", so here's hoping they see the light of day sooner rather than later.

Internal is band from New Bedford, MA who formed in 2020, from the looks of things.  Internal features Trevor Vaughn, who's best known for playing in the band Wound Man, so going on that alone, you know you're in for something truly special.  Internal play an abrasive, harsh, and brutal as fuck style of hardcore, punk, and powerviolence.  Since forming in 2020, Internal have released a self-titled EP in May of 2020.  Scrape is the band's latest EP, which was released on June 7th, 2020.  On Scrape, Internal offer up ten tracks of vicious, scathing, and brutal as fuck sounding hardcore, punk, and powerviolence.  Overall, Scrape makes for an awesome listen and definitely should not be missed.  Highly recommended!  Enjoy!

Permanent Makeup is a three piece band from Tampa, Florida who formed in 2011, from the looks of things.  Permanent Makeup play a tense and discordant style of music that incorporates elements of punk and post punk within their sound.  Musically, Permanent Makeup can be said to be influenced by bands such as Unwound, Shellac, Red Monkey, and Polvo.  Since forming in 2011, Permanent Makeup have released a self-titled eight song EP in April of 2011, a seven song EP titled Live On WWNFN 2011 in December of 2011, an eight song EP titled Live On WMNF 2012 in December of 2012, a twelve song LP titled The Void...It Creeps in February of 2013, a three song 7" titled Gibbering in January of 2014, a thirteen song LP titled Taker in August of 2015, and a ten song LP titled I Don't Like You either in July of 2017.  Scrape is the band's latest full-length LP, which was released via Dead Tank records on October 6th, 2017.  On Scrape, Permanent Makeup offer up fifteen tracks of tense and discordant sounding punk and post punk.  Overall, Scrape makes for a killer listen and definitely should not be missed.  Highly recommended!  Enjoy!

I can't mention Mi Amore and other Canadian hardcore bands without also heaping massive amounts of praise upon Quebec's COBRA NOIR. Also existing in the mid-late 2000's, this band did their part in laying the groundwork for every good hardcore band you hear today. Half of their stuff is damn near impossible to find, digitally or physically, but I managed to scrape together their 2 LP's and a few more at the links above. Their first LP, Abode Of The Dead (2005), is about as close in feel and tone to Cursed as you are going to find in a record. You should be downloading this shit at this point. Their next LP, Barricades (2006), seems almost purposefully under-produced in comparison, but for any fan of Coliseum or Heartless, this is a joy to hear. Listening to these records today, they are still completely and absolutely relevant. It's hard to believe they were recorded almost a decade ago. And if you happen to have MP3's of their Demonstration, Self-Titled or Last Days split 7", please let us know.
